macros.name: added
macros.doc: The command \added{<text>}{<number >} flags the position of the additional <text> and highlights it.

macros.name: bibannex
macros.doc: The command \bibannex starts an informative section of the document entitled ‘Bibliography’.

macros.name: bref
macros.doc: For the purposes of ISO documents, the command \bref{<ref >} is supplied which properly formats a bibliographic reference.

macros.name: captionsize
macros.doc: The size of the captioning font is controlled by the value of the \captionsize command.

macros.name: clause
macros.doc: The command to start a new clause.

macros.name: contcaption
macros.doc: The \contcaption command can be used to put a ‘continuation’ caption into a float.

macros.name: copyrightnotice
macros.doc: The required English text of the copyright notice.

macros.name: definition
macros.doc: Within a definitions environment the command \definition{⟨phrase⟩}{⟨definition text⟩} is used to specify and define each term.

macros.name: deleted
macros.doc: The command \deleted{<number >} flags the position of deleted text.

macros.name: extrahead
macros.doc: \extrahead puts its contents into the page header (e.g., a document number).

macros.name: fcandaclause
macros.doc: This macro starts a clause ‘Fundamental concepts and assumptions’.

macros.name: fwdbp
macros.doc: The command \fwdbp prints the ISO specified boilerplate for the initial paragraphs of a foreword.

macros.name: fwdnopatents
macros.doc: \fwdnopatents is the boilerplate for the Foreword paragraph dealing with potential patent rights.

macros.name: ifpdf
macros.doc: The class provides a command, \ifpdf, to test whether or not the document is being processed by LaTeX or by pdfLaTeX.

macros.name: indexspace
macros.doc: The command \indexspace can be used to add space between the entries.

macros.name: intropatents
macros.doc: The \intropatents prints some of the patent boilerplate that may be required in the Introduction.

macros.name: isourl
macros.doc: The command \isourl{<text>} can be used for typesetting <text> as an URL address.

macros.name: languageofedition
macros.doc: The command \languageofedition{<code>} is used to identify the language of the edition.

macros.name: listoffigures
macros.doc: This macro is used to request that LaTeX produces a list of figures.

macros.name: listoftables
macros.doc: This macro is used to request that LaTeX produces a list of tables.

macros.name: maxsecnumdepth
macros.doc: \maxsecnumdepth{<sec>} sets the level at which clauses will be numbered.

macros.name: maxtocdepth
macros.doc: \maxtocdepth{<sec>} sets the level at which clauses will be put into the ToC.

macros.name: moved
macros.doc: The command \moved{<text>}{<number >} flags the position of moved <text> and highlights it.

macros.name: normrefbp
macros.doc: The command \normrefbp{<document identifier>} prints the ISO required text for the introduction to the listing of normative references.

macros.name: normrefsclause
macros.doc: The \normrefsclause command starts a new numbered clause called ‘Normative references’, which is given the label ;i2.

macros.name: reference
macros.doc: This is a three parameter command for printing an informatively listed reference document.

macros.name: scopeclause
macros.doc: The \scopeclause command starts a new numbered clause called ‘Scope’, which is given the label ;i1.

macros.name: setsecnumdepth
macros.doc: \setsecnumdepth{⟨sec⟩} is the user command for setting secnumdepth to the value for ⟨sec⟩.

macros.name: settocdepth
macros.doc: \settocdepth{⟨sec⟩} is the user command for setting tocdepth in the .toc file to the value corresponding to ⟨sec⟩.

macros.name: standard
macros.doc: The command \standard{<number of standard>} is used to identify the standard.

macros.name: symboldef
macros.doc: Within a symbols environment the command \symboldef{⟨symbol⟩}{⟨meaning⟩} is used to specify and explain each symbol or abbreviation.

macros.name: title
macros.doc: The command to produce the title of the standard is \title{<intro>}{<main>}{<compl >}.

envs.name: anexample
envs.doc: The environment \begin{anexample} <text> \end{anexample} produces an un-numbered example whose body consists of <text>.

envs.name: anote
envs.doc: The environment \begin{anote} <text> \end{anote} produces an un-numbered note whose body consists of <text>.

envs.name: cover
envs.doc: The cover environment is for typesetting an informal cover sheet. there is no restriction on what can go into it, except that if used it must be the first element in the document and the contents must not exceed a single page.

envs.name: example
envs.doc: The environment \begin{example} <text> \end{example} produces a numbered example whose body consists of <text>.

envs.name: foreword
envs.doc: The foreword environment specifies that a table of contents, list of figures and list of tables be produced, and starts a new unnumbered clause called Foreword.

envs.name: inscope
envs.doc: The inscope and outofscope environments are provided for itemized listing of elements that are within and outside the scope of the standard.

envs.name: introduction
envs.doc: The introduction environment starts a new unnumbered clause called ‘Introduction’ with one column formatting.

envs.name: note
envs.doc: The environment \begin{note} <text> \end{note} produces a numbered note whose body consists of <text>.

envs.name: nreferences
envs.doc: The nreferences environment is for listing normative references.

envs.name: olddefinitions
envs.doc: The olddefinitions environment is for listing terms which have been defined in some other standard.

envs.name: outofscope
envs.doc: The inscope and outofscope environments are provided for itemized listing of elements that are within and outside the scope of the standard.

envs.name: quote
envs.doc: The quote environment is like the quotation environment except that paragraphs are not indented.

envs.name: references
envs.doc: Informative bibliography elements are listed in the references environment.

envs.name: theindex
envs.doc: The theindex environment is used for printing an index.
